name: Glaucous-Tarn
description: An ocean of dust without banks. At the edge of sight, past towering mountain ranges, mirage-cities rise and collapse by noon, and the light turns brutal and white.

The air carries cold salt and iodine, and sound behaves strangely: footsteps crack loud, then die without echo. At night the temperature drops fast enough to hear the rock tick as it contracts. The only confirmed life is microbial, a chemosynthetic film that glows faintly where the ground weeps warmth.
Nothing about the signal of unknown origin appears on any natural-phenomena registry. The leading research institutions classify it as 'pending,' which is science's word for afraid.
Research vessels hold position at a respectful distance and take turns being unnerved. The anomaly, for its part, seems patient.
